answer: Sybil resistance depends on epoch-bound enclave commitments. Each agent seals a keypair in hardware and posts a cipher of its measurement plus a bond; the epoch seed mixes a delta into the nonce, so old ciphertexts decrypt to nothing and replay dies. Each close the ledger draws a marble without replacement, re-executes it, and matches measurements. Accounts sharing a measurement collide; the shared bond burns rather than refunds. A thousand identities cost a thousand enclaves plus capital lost at first collision, and a replay forfeits a full epoch of work; marginal cost stays above emission.
